name: Bamboo
intro: Bamboo is a giant grass. It is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: Bamboo is a giant grass, not a tree.
Its stems are tall and hollow inside.
The stems have rings called joints.
Branches and leaves grow from the joints.
Some bamboo is small, and some is taller than a house.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Wild bamboo grows in Asia, Africa, and the Americas.
Many kinds grow where it is warm all year.
Other kinds can live where winters are cold.
Bamboo often grows close together in big clumps.
One bamboo plant can spread into a whole forest.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: Bamboo needs plenty of light.
It needs soil that drains well.
It needs water, but not too much.
Warm-weather bamboo can die if it freezes.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: New bamboo stems are called shoots.
Shoots come up from stems under the ground.
A shoot grows straight up very fast.
Some bamboo can grow as tall as a first grader in one day!
Most bamboo makes flowers only once in many years.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Giant pandas eat almost nothing but bamboo.
Red pandas and some lemurs eat bamboo too.
People build houses and bridges with bamboo.
Bamboo can be made into paper, chopsticks, and cloth.
Bamboo grows back quickly after it is cut.
